newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Bund vol to ride out U.S. employment data.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Bund vol to ride out U.S. employment data.

text.p: Implied volatility of Bund options will survive any surprise U.S. employment data on Friday without a sharp spike higher, options brokers said.
"Even if the data are very high, volatility won't go up that much because the erosion is quite expensive," said one broker from a French bank on the LIFFE floor.
Erosion, or time decay, is a major factor in options pricing. Time decay has a strong impact on the price of an option going into a weekend.
Bund options volatility was steady, quoted in a 5.43-5.65 percent range for July options exercisable into the September contract, the French broker said.
August options were quoted at 5.54-5.64 percent, September at 5.44-5.55 percent and December at 5.45-5.55 percent.
The last U.S. employment data before the next Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) in early July will be released at 1230 GMT.

Non-farm payrolls will rise 219,000 for the five-week period of May, according to a Reuters survey. Traders on LIFFE were forecasting a wide range of figures on Friday, from an increase of 150,000 to one of 300,000, and said the market would also be watching closely for revisions to previous months' data.
"There won't be more than 1-1/2 points on the price of a straddle (after the figures)," the broker said. "No one wants to go into the weekend long."
The September Bund future was trading at 101.42 at 1020 GMT.
One broker from a U.S. bank on LIFFE saw a short-lived rise in Bund volatility if payrolls were significantly higher.
"There will be a kneejerk reaction as the market absorbs the statistics, but then it will come back down again. Most of the big houses are keeping to the sidelines."
Among Friday's trades, 1,000 lots changed hands in August 104.00 calls. Dealers said the trade was a purchase by one house, and was thought to be a hedge for a short cash position.
